h1: Creating Green and Sustainable Playgrounds: A Model for India's Future

props.title: Creating Green and Sustainable Playgrounds: A Model for India's Future
props.summaryText: Sustainability in playgrounds is mostly about building things that last and working with nature: durable equipment, trees, rainwater, local manufacturing and good upkeep.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Children playing on purple and green play equipment at a school

takeaways.text: The most sustainable playground is one that lasts: durable materials and good maintenance beat frequent replacement.
Trees and shade lower temperatures and make play areas usable for more of the year.
Manage rainwater with drained surfaces, permeable paths and planting.
Local manufacturing reduces transport and makes spares and repairs easier.

faq.a: A playground designed to last a long time with low maintenance, built with durable materials, integrated with trees and planting, managing rainwater well, and supplied and serviced locally so parts can be repaired rather than replaced.

faq.q: Are recycled materials better for playgrounds?
faq.a: Recycled content can reduce environmental impact, but durability and safety come first. A recycled part that fails early is not sustainable. Ask about both recycled content and expected life.

faq.q: How do trees make playgrounds more sustainable?
faq.a: Trees shade equipment and surfaces, lower temperatures, absorb rainwater, improve air quality and make play areas usable for more of the year, reducing the need for built shade.
